::: {.why}
Six strategies compared in phase 6 means six result objects that have to be identical in shape, and defining that shape now is cheaper than converting later.
:::

## What you should be able to do tonight

- Define a result object carrying returns, positions, fills, costs, metadata and the trial record, and serialise it.
- Produce a tearsheet from the result object alone, with no access to the engine.

## Tasks <span class='task-total'>60 min</span>

::: {.task-list}
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [30 min]{.task-min} Define the result in qlib/backtest/result.py: daily returns, positions, fills, a cost breakdown by component, the configuration that produced it, the code version, and the research log entry id. Serialise it to disk so a result can be reloaded a month later without rerunning.
:::
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [30 min]{.task-min} Build the tearsheet from it: equity curve, drawdown, rolling Sharpe with the interval from qlib/stats.py, turnover, exposure, and the cost breakdown. Compare your output against what pyfolio-reloaded produces on the same returns to check you have not missed a standard panel.
:::
:::

## The running strategy

::: {.project}
Every backtest now returns one serialisable result object carrying its own configuration and code version, and the tearsheet is built from that object alone. Reproducing a figure from March in July becomes a file read rather than a rerun.
:::
